instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the lower third. Pat the 2 lbs pork dry and cut it into 4 big chunks. Rub them all over with 1 1/4 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper.
Stir the 1 1/2 tsp oregano, 1 tsp of the cumin and 1 tbsp of the oil together in a small bowl and rub it over the pork.
Cut the onion in half. Chop one half. Cut the other half into two quarters and set them aside for later. Peel and smash 2 of the garlic cloves. Juice the orange. That should be about 1/3 cup.
Put the chopped onion and the smashed garlic in a Dutch oven and set the pork on top, fat side up. Pour the orange juice and 1 cup water around it. Cover and roast for 2 hours.

Take the lid off and roast for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until the top is browned and a chunk pulls apart easily with a fork. If you have a thermometer, you're cooking it to about 195°F in the middle. Add a splash of water if the pot looks dry. There should be about 1 cup of juice left at the end.

Meanwhile, heat the broiler with a rack about 5 inches below it. Peel the husks off the 1 lb tomatillos, rinse off the sticky coating and cut them in half. Put them cut side down on a foil lined baking sheet with the poblano, the jalapeño, one of the onion quarters and the last garlic clove, still in its skin.
Broil for 8 to 10 minutes, turning the peppers once, until the tomatillos are blistered and soft and the peppers are blackened in spots. Let them cool for a few minutes.

Pull the stems and seeds out of the poblano and jalapeño and squeeze the garlic out of its skin. Transfer everything from the baking sheet to a blender with any juices. Add a big handful of the cilantro, the juice of 1 lime, the remaining 1/2 tsp cumin and the last 1/2 tsp salt. Pulse until it's mostly smooth with a little texture. That should be about 2 cups. Pour it into a bowl for the table.
When the pork is done, lift it onto a cutting board and shred it with two forks, pulling out any big pieces of fat. Skim the fat off the juices in the pot.

Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over high. Add half the pork in a thin layer and drizzle it with a few spoonfuls of the juices. Leave it alone for 3 to 4 minutes, until the juices have cooked off and the bottom is golden and crisp. Flip it and cook the other side for 1 minute. Transfer it to a platter and crisp the rest the same way.
Meanwhile, finely dice the last onion quarter, thinly slice 4 or 5 of the radishes, chop a little more cilantro and cut the other lime into wedges. Crumble the cotija.
Warm the 12 tortillas in a dry skillet over medium for about 30 seconds a side and wrap them in a clean towel.
Drizzle the pork with the rest of the juices. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.
Serve the pork in the warm tortillas with the green tomatillo sauce, onion, radishes, cilantro, cotija and lime wedges.
method_notes: RecipeTin Eats leads with its carnitas, which rubs pork shoulder with salt, pepper, oregano, cumin and oil, cooks it over onion, garlic, jalapeño and orange juice until it shreds, then crisps it in batches in a hot pan with its own juices; its oven method roasts it covered at 325°F for 2 hours and uncovered for 1 to 1 1/2 hours. None of the salsa verde pork pages had 20 ratings, so the salsa comes from Fannetastic Food, which chars tomatillos, poblano, jalapeño and onion and blends them with lime, cilantro and cumin. Foodiecrush braises pork butt in jarred salsa verde with broth, cumin, coriander and oregano, crisps it in a 400°F oven and tops the tacos with cotija, pickled onion and cilantro. This follows RecipeTin's oven method at half its size, moves the jalapeño out of the pot into the salsa so the pork stays mild, and broils the salsa vegetables instead of grilling them.
